xref.title: Lawsuit Against Napster (2000)
xref.body: Metallica, notably with drummer Lars Ulrich as the public face, filed a lawsuit against Napster on April 30, 2000, after discovering their unreleased demo "I Disappear" and their entire catalog were being freely traded online. Lars Ulrich physically delivered a 60,000-page list of 335,435 alleged Metallica song pirates to Napster's offices. The band sought at least $10 million in damages, a ban for all users trading Metallica songs, and university crackdowns on student downloading. This action generated intense fan backlash, damaging Metallica's reputation as "rich rock stars, bullying fans." Despite this, Napster was ultimately shut down in July 2001 after settling with Metallica and Dr. Dre, confirming that its practices violated copyright. xref.title: Mainstream Reach Comparison
xref.body: Taylor Swift's mainstream appeal is used as a comparative example to illustrate how the concept of "mainstream" has changed. It's suggested that if she existed in 1995, her music would be inescapable daily, making it easy for anyone to name multiple singles. However, in the fragmented post-2000 music landscape, only her dedicated fans ("swifties") would easily recall three singles, demonstrating how even major stars now inhabit a more niche role within a diverse music culture. "If this were 1995, Taylor would have been way more popular than she is today and everyone. I mean, everyone would have been exposed to her music daily. So answering that question, naming three singles, would have been very easy."

xref.title: Travis Barker's Clothing Company – Famous Stars and Straps
xref.body: Travis Barker, drummer for blink-182, founded the clothing company Famous Stars and Straps in 1999, based in Corona, California. The brand targets the skate crowd and offers t-shirts, jackets, and hats for men, along with shirts, pants, and bikinis for women, in addition to accessories like belt buckles and bandanas. The company's success is bolstered by famous friends, including Tim Armstrong of Rancid, Steve-O of Sum 41, members of Avenged Sevenfold, and B-Real of Cypress Hill, who wear the brand publicly. Famous Stars and Straps generates millions in annual revenue, and its presence is notable at events like the Warped Tour. "He founded the company in 1999 and targeted the Skate Crowd."
